Locus Robotics and Kimball Midwest win supply-chain robotics award

A deployment across three distribution centres has supported more than 13.2 million picks, with the companies reporting productivity gains and payback within a year.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗18 September 2026English editorial summary
Story

Recognition for a working warehouse deployment

Locus Robotics and Kimball Midwest received the Best Use of Robotics award at the 2026 Supply Chain Excellence Awards USA. The project started in Columbus in January 2024 and expanded to three sites within 14 months without major changes to existing shelving.

A fleet of more than 100 robots

Autonomous mobile robots support picking and putaway at distribution centres in Ohio, Texas and Nevada. According to the companies, the deployment has supported more than 13.2 million robot-assisted picks and approximately one million putaway transactions.

Productivity and payback

Picking rates rose from around 110 to more than 160 lines per hour, while putaway increased from about 30 to 91–96 lines per hour. The companies report payback within a year, shorter employee training and less reliance on temporary labour.

Moving staff between changing priorities

Using the same platform for both picking and putaway allows staff to move between tasks as demand changes. The aim is to support growth while maintaining the promise to ship orders received before 4 p.m. on the same day.
